label: Person
name: Achille Locatelli
summary:
Achille Locatelli (1856–1935) was an Italian Catholic cardinal and Vatican diplomat who served as papal nuncio to several European countries and later as Secretary of the Sacred Congregation for Extraordinary Ecclesiastical Affairs — one of the most important positions in the Vatican's foreign policy apparatus. Born in Bergamo, he was ordained a priest and entered the Vatican diplomatic service, rising through a series of nunciatures.

Locatelli's diplomatic career spanned one of the most turbulent periods in modern Church-state relations: the Kulturkampf's aftermath in Germany, the French anti-clerical Third Republic, the collapse of the old European order in World War I, and the post-war reconstruction of the European state system. Vatican diplomacy during this period required exceptional skill in navigating hostile governments while maintaining the Church's institutional interests.

His elevation to the cardinalate by Pope Benedict XV placed him within the inner circle of Vatican governance at a moment when the Church was attempting to construct a new framework for its international relations in the post-war world. His career in the Congregation for Extraordinary Ecclesiastical Affairs put him at the heart of the Vatican's most sensitive international negotiations during the 1910s–1920s.
